PLANTED_INCONSISTENCY.description: The narrative promises 120 youth served with a 1:10 mentor ratio, which requires 12 mentors. The budget funds 2 mentors at 0.5 FTE. The two documents cannot both be true.

conflicting_sources.quoted_text: Riverbend will serve 120 youth at a 1:10 mentor-to-participant ratio.

proposed_resolutions: Reduce the served-youth target to 20 to match funded mentor capacity.
Increase the mentor budget line to fund 12 mentors (requires cutting elsewhere or raising the request).
Restate the ratio as a small-group model with documented staffing math.
PLANTED_INCONSISTENCY.why_this_one: It is the single check that proves the thesis: the application and the compliance object are the same thing. An org that submits this wins a grant it cannot perform, and the performance report at month 6 is where it explodes.

AWARD_DELTAS_TO_SURFACE.downstream_effect: Stipend plan must be re-scoped from 120 to ~72 participants, OR the per-participant amount cut. Moving these funds to another category requires prior approval under 200.308.

AWARD_DELTAS_TO_SURFACE.agency_note: Equipment purchases require prior written approval.
AWARD_DELTAS_TO_SURFACE.downstream_effect: Ledger Sentinel must block laptop purchases until an approval artifact exists.
Convening target PP-3 of 4 events is now underfunded — a performance promise the award silently made unachievable. Nobody's software catches this today.

ledger_stream.note: Fired in order on demand. Each is chosen to land on a DIFFERENT determination value — that is the point. Seven determinations, seven visibly different behaviors.

transactions.memo: Fall community convening — catering for 80, incl. wine service
transactions.expected_behavior: SPLIT — $412.00 alcohol carved out as presumptively_unallowable under 200.423 and proposed for reclass to unrestricted funds. The remaining $828.00 is NOT auto-approved; it routes for program-purpose review under 200.432/200.438 against obligation for convening PP-3.

transactions.citation_note: Verified 2026-08-26. Was 200.334 + 200.474. Adequate documentation is 200.403(g); 200.334 is the three-year retention duration and is the wrong hook for a cost that never had a receipt. Travel is 200.475; 200.474 is Transportation costs, meaning goods.

transactions.note: Riverbend runs three programs out of this building. Charging 100% to the award is the single most common real-world finding.
Blocks against specific condition SC-2. Sentinel must cite the AWARD TERM, not just the CFR — that is the provenance chain doing visible work.
transactions.citation_note: Verified 2026-08-26, determination aligned to DEMO_SCRIPT.md. At $1,600 per unit these laptops sit BELOW the 200.439(b)(2) $10,000 special-purpose prior-approval threshold, and 200.453(c) expressly allows charging computing devices as direct costs when essential and allocable but not solely dedicated. 2 CFR therefore does NOT block this purchase - award term SC-2 does. That is why the value is conflicts_with_award_terms and not requires_prior_approval: the conflict is with the award, not the regulation. The Sentinel must lead with SC-2 and cite the CFR as context.

transactions.note: Dated BEFORE period of performance start (2026-10-01). Pre-award cost.
transactions.citation_note: Verified 2026-08-26, determination aligned to DEMO_SCRIPT.md. 200.458 makes pre-award costs allowable only to the extent they would have been allowable after the start date AND only with the written approval of the Federal agency - that is requires_prior_approval on a plain reading. 200.403(h) supplies the budget-period requirement. Dated 2026-09-18, before the 2026-10-01 period-of-performance start.

transactions.note: Turns on whether this organization's primary purpose includes lobbying. An agent cannot know that. It asks, with the exact question stated.
transactions.citation_note: Verified 2026-08-26. The escalation is correctly founded. 200.454(c) makes civic and community organization memberships ALLOWABLE outright, so 'chamber dues' is not suspicious on its face; 200.454(e) makes memberships unallowable only where the organization's PRIMARY PURPOSE is lobbying. That is a fact about the organization, not about the invoice, which is exactly why a human has to answer it. Do not say chamber dues need prior approval - they do not.
